content: Spouses married during marriage purchased property in Monte San Pietro under legal community regime, separated 2008, civil marriage effects terminated May 2023. Wife sought dissolution and assignment of husband's ownership share to settle his maintenance debt (€137,423.38 unpaid from separation agreements). Husband declared default. Articles 191, 720, 810, 812, 813 Italian Civil Code govern community dissolution upon separation, indivisible property allocation, and asset definitions. Issue concerned proper remedy for indivisible property where mortgage registration encumbers one co-owner's share for unpaid maintenance obligations. Mandatory mediation attempted, interrupted September 2023. Documentary evidence established co-ownership and husband's maintenance failures: €1,200 monthly for children plus €800 for wife per separation agreements; subsequent amendment reduced wife's maintenance to €500 monthly (December 2019) with children financially independent. Husband's bankruptcy proceedings (2010) declared extinguished August 2017 insufficient assets—unsuccessful debt recovery. Total claim €137,423.38 plus execution costs €3,615.70 (total €141,039.08). Mortgage registration on husband's share pursuant to separation appearance October 2008 encumbers property. Article 720 applicable where indivisible assets require sacrificing individual portion allocation to preserve functionality and economic value. Market value derived from parties' mediation expert reports mathematical average: plaintiff's expert €278,239, defendant's expert €313,000, average €295,619.50. Each 50% share €147,809.75. Husband's share only concrete resource for obligation fulfillment. Property assigned entirely to wife to definitively resolve prolonged legal situation and avoid litigation proliferation. Wife pays husband €6,770.67 (difference between share value €147,809.75 and credit €141,039.08). Assignment satisfies maintenance claim through property allocation rather than continued enforcement proceedings. Losing party bears costs per Article 91 including technical consultancy advance.
